title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Nvidia beat Q2 revenue/EPS estimates; shares dipped slightly after-hours Wednesday but Nasdaq 100 futures jumped ~1% Thursday after CFO Colette Kress signaled strong FY2028 sales growth, easing AI-spending-slowdown fears
Markets: US stocks traded mixed Wednesday (Dow -0.2%, S&P/Nasdaq slipped) as sticky inflation kept traders cautious ahead of the Fed's Jackson Hole gathering; gold fell ~1%, oil eased near $82/bbl
Companies: Meta settled child-safety suits with 48 state AGs for roughly $17-18B, agreeing to new teen limits (2-hr daily cap, overnight-use ban for under-18s); shares rose ~1.1%
Companies: Vanguard agreed to acquire fintech custodian Altruist for ~$4B, challenging Schwab/Fidelity in independent-advisor services; Schwab shares fell 2.6%
Companies: Google Cloud is rolling out pay-as-you-go pricing for Gemini Enterprise to ease corporate 'AI sticker shock'

Macro/Policy: Fed's preferred inflation gauge (core PCE) held at 3.7% y/y in July, above forecast and well above the 2% target; Boston Fed's Collins warned rates may need to rise further if inflation doesn't cool

Macro/Policy: Bill Gates published a stark essay warning the AI transition could be 'one of the most turbulent' periods in history, urging a robot tax and jobs reserved for humans; Bank of Korea hiked to 3.00% while the RBA held at 4.35%
